project.title: Projectplaner
project.description: A local graph-first planning tool where aspects, tasks and relationships stay navigable.

metadata.purpose: Make project planning addressable, explainable and conflict-checkable.

entities.title: Agent Workflow Contracts

metadata.purpose: Define how agents communicate with Projectplaner and each other.
metadata.userValue: Agents spend fewer tokens rediscovering context and leave useful state for successors.
metadata.behavior: Workflows are graph-attached flow entities; packets and playbooks are reference entities; tasks use these contracts for handoff.
nonGoals: No new schema tables in v1
No automatic subagent spawning in v1
No MCP server in this slice
metadata.acceptanceShape: An agent can find relevant work, consume compact context, execute a task, and leave a packet without rereading broad repo context.

entities.title: Agent Orientation Workflow
entities.summary: Select the right graph target before implementation work.
entities.body: Agents query Projectplaner, broaden once when sparse, select the most specific Aspect, Feature, or Task target, and report confidence before continuing.

metadata.trigger: Agent receives a user request or starts a Projectplaner task.
steps: Query Projectplaner with the request terms
If sparse, broaden once using nearby product concepts
Select the most specific Aspect, Feature, or Task target
metadata.success: Agent has a selected target, relevant entities, missing context, and next workflow.
metadata.failure: Agent asks the user only when graph search and one broadened query still leave target choice unsafe.

entities.title: Task Consumption Handoff Workflow
entities.summary: Consume compact task handoff context before broad repo reading.
entities.body: Agents read the task, primary target, linked packets, and listed anchors first; they broaden only when packet context is stale or insufficient.

metadata.trigger: Agent is handed an existing task or task ID.
steps: Read the primary Aspect or Feature target
Broaden search only when packet anchors are stale or insufficient
metadata.success: Agent decides continue, reorient, or ask_user and names the next action.
metadata.failure: Agent writes why the packet was insufficient before broadening context.

entities.title: Execution Result Workflow
entities.summary: Leave compact implementation results for the next agent.
entities.body: Agents record changed files, verification, facts, remaining work, blockers, and next action in a compact packet when implementation completes or pauses.

metadata.trigger: Agent completes or pauses scoped implementation work.
steps: Record changed files and commands run
Update or create a compact packet for the next agent
metadata.success: Next agent can continue from the packet without reading the prior chat.
metadata.failure: Packet records blockers and whether user input is required.

entities.title: Orientation Packet v1
entities.summary: Compact machine-oriented schema for agent handoff packets.
entities.body: Defines the minimal packet fields agents should read and write when handing off task context: workflow, state, targets, anchors, facts, already-checked context, next action, avoid list, open questions, confidence, and updatedAt.

facts: The CLI owns the first agent-facing workflow surface.
alreadyChecked: No dedicated workflow schema exists in v1.
example.next: Read this packet and continue from the listed anchors.
avoid: Do not reread broad seed data unless changing bootstrap fixtures.

metadata.style: Compact machine-oriented JSON, not a prose context dump.

entities.title: Agent Playbook v1
entities.summary: Short agent-facing rules for using Projectplaner as compact handoff memory.
entities.body: Orient first, consume linked packets before broad reading, attach all tasks to Aspect or Feature targets, and leave compact deltas for successors.

instructions: Orient in Projectplaner before code changes
Run Projectplaner CLI calls serially; do not parallelize orient, packet-read, packet-write, or relation writes against SQLite
Read task and primary target first
Read linked orientation packets before broad repo search
Every new task must link to an Aspect or Feature
Write compact deltas, not transcript summaries
defaultStart: Read primary Aspect/Feature from task relation
Do the smallest scoped work for acceptance criteria
operationalConstraints: Projectplaner currently uses local SQLite through short-lived CLI processes.
Agents must serialize Projectplaner CLI calls to avoid database is locked failures.
Parallel file reads are fine; parallel Projectplaner DB commands are not.
metadata.futureStorageDirection: When multi-agent concurrency or semantic orientation needs grow, investigate a Dockerized Postgres backend with pgvector rather than replacing the planning graph with a vector database.
nonGoals: Do not require automatic subagent spawning
Do not replace human-readable AGENTS.md yet
Do not create large handoff essays

doNotReread: large prose transcript summaries in packets

Tasks must be executable later without the originating chat; the immediate deliverable of the loop is a navigable plan, not code.

xyflow workflow mode + flow.metadata graph + per-task context bag
metadata.decision: xyflow workflow mode + flow.metadata graph + per-task context bag
metadata.rationale: Reuses known editor, keeps plans inspectable in Projectplaner, lets runners parse node data without serving giant prompts, and scopes memory to each Task for small models and multiple iterations.

LLM never receives the whole workflow, only current node responsibility + declared reads

entities.title: Workflow Step Graph v1
entities.summary: v1 schema for workflow nodes/edges, per-task context bags, and tool↔LLM dataflow.
entities.body: Defines how workflow step graphs are stored on flow entities, how per-task context bags move data between tool and LLM nodes, and what each node type may declare. Enrich later; this is the v1 lock.

principles: Tool/function nodes run without LLM and write structured values into declared writes.
LLM nodes receive only: node instructions + reads subset + optional tiny system preamble. Never the whole workflow graph.
Every node declares reads[] and writes[]. Undeclared bag keys are invisible to that node.
Auto context/filter nodes populate the bag before any LLM call.
Between tool and LLM: tools write canonical JSON under writes; LLM reads those keys only. Prefer tool output schemas over prose.
If a step fails validation of writes, stop or route via gate — do not dump errors into unconstrained chat.
toolToLlm: Tool node writes e.g. matches, filteredEntities, createdEntityId
Edge advances to LLM node with reads: ["goal","filteredEntities"]
LLM returns only declared writes e.g. chosenAspectId, rationale
Next tool/write node consumes chosenAspectId without re-asking LLM for full history

llm.instructions: Pick the smallest truthful Aspect id from filteredEntities, or say createNew with a title.

storage.instructions: llm.instructions inline on node, or llm.instructionRef -> reference entity for alternate/reusable prompts
storage.ui: xyflow positions on nodes; Aspect Graph mode remains separate

metadata.style: Compact machine-oriented JSON on flow + task metadata. Nodes hold enough data to parse; runners do not need to serve the whole graph to an LLM.

dataFields.auto: Deterministic ops for context/filter nodes (loadContext, filter, assign) — no LLM
dataFields.gate: askUserIf / stopIf / route expressions over bag keys
dataFields.llm: instructions or instructionRef, tools allowlist, inputKeys, outputSchema
dataFields.reads: bag keys visible to this node
dataFields.title: Human label
dataFields.tool: Function/MCP tool invocation: name + argsFromBag mapping
dataFields.write: Graph write helper for entity create/update when not using generic tool node

workflowEdge.label: optional route name e.g. default | sparse | failed
